sources.title: Pulse of the industry: Medical technology report 2021
key_facts: MedTech achieved record revenues of US$446 billion in 2020, marking its fourth successive year of growth at 6.3%.
MedTech revenue growth for the first half of 2021 was over 16%, demonstrating sector resilience.
R&D spending reached US$23.8 billion in 2020, representing the highest annual growth rate (+17.2%) since before the 2007 financial crisis.
Total equity investment in MedTech reached a new peak of US$34 billion, comprising US$9 billion VC, US$6 billion IPO, US$4 billion SPAC, and US$16 billion follow-on.
MedTech Emerging Leaders (companies with revenues below US$500 million) saw a 128% rise in valuations between January 2020 and August 2021.
MedTech valuations outperformed Pharma and Biotech by more than 50%.
Over the 12 months ending June 2021, MedTech companies executed 288 M&A deals, the highest annual number since EY began the Pulse report in 2007.
The industry attracted US$9.1 billion in VC in the 12-month period to June 2021, up 34% over the previous year and the highest level in the past decade.
The non-imaging-diagnostics segment recorded a 24% annual growth rate in 2020, largely driven by pandemic-related demand.
94% of commercial leaders and conglomerates that reported first-half 2021 financials improved their revenues compared to 2020.
Baxter signed a US$10.5 billion deal to acquire connected care specialist Hillrom in September 2021.
Philips purchased BioTelemetry, a maker of digital patient monitoring platforms and AI-based analytics, for US$2.8 billion.
Boston Scientific announced a US$1.3 billion buy-out of Preventice Solutions, which designs remote monitoring services and mobile health solutions for cardiac arrhythmia patients.
Siemens Healthineers acquired Varian Medical Systems for US$16.4 billion, primarily to build scale in oncology.
The US Centers for Medicare & Medicaid Services introduced the Acute Hospital Care At Home program, adopted by 53 health systems and 116 hospitals across 29 states as of April 2021.
COVID-19 accelerated the shift of health care delivery away from traditional clinic and hospital settings toward home and telehealth settings.
EY identifies five key areas for MedTech business model transformation: patient-centric care, out-of-hospital care, data strategy, regulatory reform, and supply chain resilience.

sources.title: 2026 Life sciences outlook | Deloitte Insights
key_facts: More than 75% of responding biopharma and medtech executives are confident in their own organizations' financial outlooks for 2026.
Only 41% of surveyed life sciences executives feel optimistic about the health of the global economy.
Surveyed medtech executives tend to be more optimistic about the future than their biopharma peers, while anticipating similar revenue growth of 81%.
There is no statistically significant difference between the growth expectations of medtech executives in the United States (84%) and those in several countries outside the United States (78%).
Only 22% of life sciences leaders said they have successfully scaled AI, and just 9% reported achieving significant returns on AI efforts.
One-third of respondents (33%) said connected care delivery is a top trend for 2026, a rise of 15 percentage points year over year.
35% of respondents cited customer adoption of digital tools as a key trend for 2026.
A supply chain executive from a large US medtech company noted a shortage of phlebotomists and lab managers, and a need to automate and make processes cost-effective.
The survey included 280 C-suite executives from biopharma and medtech companies across the United States, Europe (France, Germany, Switzerland, and the United Kingdom), and Asia (China and Japan).
The Deloitte US Center for Health Solutions conducted its fourth annual Life Sciences Outlook Survey from August to September 2025.
market_data_points: 90% of biopharma leaders in surveyed European and Asian countries report 'positive' or 'cautiously positive' expectations for 2026.
83% of surveyed European and Asian biopharma leaders predict steady or strong revenue growth for 2026, with only 2% anticipating a decline.
56% of US-based biopharma leaders express a positive or cautiously positive outlook for 2026, while 27% remain negative or uncertain.
71% of US biopharma respondents anticipate revenue gains in 2026, but 18% foresee a decline.
Medtech executives anticipate 81% revenue growth in 2026.
84% of US medtech executives anticipate revenue growth, compared to 78% of non-US medtech executives.
Nearly half of respondents (48%) identified accelerated digital transformation as a trend likely to have substantial impact in 2026, a statistically significant increase compared with 2025.
41% of respondents identified the proliferation of generative AI as an influential trend for 2026.
30% of respondents cited agentic AI as a trend influencing their organizations in 2026.
35% of respondents cited cybersecurity concerns as affecting their 2026 strategy.
44% of respondents identified pricing and access to medications, therapies, and medical technologies as major strategic considerations.
39% of respondents named geopolitical tensions as a top issue for 2026, a jump of 20 percentage points from last year.
38% of respondents identified inflation, broader economic pressures, and supply chain risks as factors shaping 2026 strategies.
37% of respondents cited increased competitive pressure from generics and biosimilars as a key 2026 trend.
26% of respondents cited expiration of blockbuster drugs and patent cliffs as a key 2026 trend.
51% of non-US respondents pointed to national regulatory changes as expected to shape organizational strategy in 2026.
36% of US respondents highlighted FDA and HHS agency restructuring as a key trend.
39% of US respondents cited economic policy changes, including tariffs, as a trend shaping 2026 strategy.
32% of respondents cited evolving customer needs and preferences as a top trend for 2026.
trend_signals: Accelerated digital transformation and AI adoption in life sciences, with generative AI and agentic AI identified as key growth drivers for 2026.
Growing interest in connected care delivery, rising 15 percentage points year-over-year to be cited by 33% of medtech executives.
Shift from a US-focused growth strategy toward a more fragmented and complex global landscape in life sciences.
Increasing automation pressure in medtech driven by labor shortages among healthcare customers.
Rising geopolitical and economic uncertainty reshaping portfolio management and market launch decisions in life sciences.
Persistent pricing and access pressures continuing to challenge medtech and biopharma commercial strategies.
Growing focus on supply chain resilience and risk management in response to inflation and geopolitical tensions.
Agentic AI—AI systems that can act autonomously—emerging as a new category of strategic interest in life sciences for 2026.
'Purposeful transformation' described as the prevailing industry posture, balancing discipline and innovation as AI matures beyond hype toward measurable productivity.
competitive_mentions: Increased competitive pressure from generics and biosimilars cited by 37% of respondents as a key trend for 2026.
Expiration of blockbuster drugs and patent cliffs cited by 26% of respondents as a competitive pressure for 2026.
regulatory_mentions: EU AI Act identified as a national regulatory change expected to affect market access, pricing, and reimbursement models for non-US life sciences companies.
Corporate Sustainability Reporting Directive (CSRD) cited as a regulatory factor shaping non-US life sciences strategies in 2026.
European Health Data Space cited as a regulatory development affecting non-US life sciences strategies.
China's volume-based procurement program cited as a regulatory factor affecting non-US life sciences market access and pricing.
FDA agency restructuring cited by 36% of US respondents as a trend shaping organizational strategy in 2026.
HHS restructuring cited by 36% of US respondents as a trend shaping organizational strategy in 2026.
US economic policy changes, including tariffs, cited by 39% of US respondents as a factor shaping 2026 strategy.

sources.title: Life Sciences & Health - Your 2026 funding roadmap
key_facts: The EU medical devices sector employs nearly one million people and is worth €170 billion.
Proposed EU medical device regulatory reforms are projected to deliver €3.3 billion in yearly savings.
Cardiovascular diseases cause 1.7 million deaths annually in the EU and cost €282 billion.
The EIC Pathfinder program funds early-stage, high-risk research at TRL 1-3 with up to €4 million at 100% funding rate, with a deadline of 12 May 2026.
The EIC Transition program supports maturation of breakthrough technologies at TRL 4-5 with up to €2.5 million at 100% funding rate, with a deadline of 16 September 2026.
The EIC Accelerator provides up to €2.5 million in grants plus €1–10 million in equity for SMEs at TRL 6-8, with up to 70% funding rate across 6 deadlines throughout 2026.
The EIC STEP initiative provides €10–30 million in equity investment for deep-tech companies at TRL 8-9 with 4 deadlines throughout 2026.
Horizon Europe Health program funds research at TRL 3-9 with €6–8 million grants at up to 70–100% funding rate, with a deadline of 16 April 2026.
The Eurostars program supports innovative SMEs with up to €500k at up to 50% funding rate, with deadlines on 19 March 2026 and October 2026.
The Innovative Health Initiative is a European public-private partnership funding collaborative research at TRL 5-8 with €5–15 million at 55% funding rate, with a deadline of 21 April 2026.
The Dutch WBSO fiscal scheme offers tax benefits for R&D activities at up to 50% of eligible costs on a year-round basis.
The Dutch Innovatiekrediet loan program provides €5–10 million in risk-bearing financing at TRL 3-8 with up to 70–100% funding rate, with a deadline of 31 December 2026.
The proposed EU Biotech Act aims to strengthen Europe's biotechnology potential by improving funding options, supporting bio-manufacturing, and easing the path from laboratory research to market.
The Safe Hearts Plan introduces the first comprehensive EU cardiovascular strategy, leveraging personalized tools, digital solutions, and an AI Incubator.
market_data_points: EU medical devices sector is worth €170 billion and employs nearly one million people.
Cardiovascular diseases cost the EU €282 billion annually and cause 1.7 million deaths per year.
Cardiovascular disease burden is projected to rise by 90% by 2050 in the EU.
Proposed EU medical device regulatory reforms are expected to deliver €3.3 billion in yearly savings.
EIC Pathfinder grants are capped at €4 million per project.
EIC Accelerator offers up to €2.5 million in grants plus €1–10 million in equity investment.
EIC STEP provides investment in the range of €10–30 million per company.
Horizon Europe Health grants range from €6–8 million per project.
Innovative Health Initiative grants range from €5–15 million per project.
Innovatiekrediet Dutch loan program provides between €5 million and €10 million per project.
trend_signals: The EU is moving toward simplified medical device regulations and streamlined single regulatory pathways for complex products.
There is a growing EU policy focus on personalized medicine, digital health, and AI solutions for cardiovascular and other diseases.
European public-private partnerships such as the Innovative Health Initiative are integrating pharmaceuticals, biotech, medical technology, and digital health into collaborative R&D.
Deep-tech scale-up support is being institutionalized in Europe through the EIC STEP initiative targeting international expansion.
EU funding programs are increasingly structured to support the full innovation lifecycle from TRL 1 through TRL 9.
Life sciences dealmaking and M&A activity are identified as key growth strategies for 2026 per EY Firepower report.
regulatory_mentions: The proposed EU Biotech Act aims to simplify regulations, accelerate clinical trial authorizations, and establish single regulatory pathways for complex products.
The Safe Hearts Plan represents the first comprehensive EU strategy for cardiovascular disease, including national plans and an AI Incubator.
Proposed EU medical device regulatory reforms aim to strengthen the EMA's role and speed up access to safe devices.
The Innovative Health Initiative is a European public-private partnership operating under EU regulatory and funding frameworks.
WBSO is a Dutch fiscal scheme governed by national R&D tax incentive regulations applicable year-round.

sources.title: 2026 Global health care outlook
key_facts: More than 80% of health system executives surveyed in Australia, Canada, Germany, the Netherlands, and the United Kingdom reported a 'positive' or 'cautiously positive' outlook for their own organizations for 2026.
72% of non-US health system executives surveyed said they were upbeat about the health care industry overall for 2026.
20% of US respondents expressed a negative industry outlook for 2026, and 33% expressed uncertainty—a notable increase from 3% who expressed uncertainty a year ago.
About 30% of surveyed health systems report operating gen AI at scale in select areas of their organizations, while just 2% have deployed AI across their entire enterprise.
About 70% of non-US health system executives expect operating revenue and margins to increase next year.
Over 50% of non-US respondents predict that operating costs will be flat or decline slightly in 2026.
64% of respondents said AI could reduce costs by standardizing and automating workflows.
55% of respondents see savings potential from increased use of predictive analytics to optimize the workforce.
49% of respondents expect benefits from tech-enabled patient engagement and remote monitoring.
Nearly half (45%) of non-US executives said care model transformation would be a leading trend in 2026.
38% of non-US respondents said their organizations would focus on preventive care and early detection in 2026.
Only 7% of US health system executives expect preventive care to be a major trend for their organizations in 2026.
More than 90% of health system executives said improving productivity would be a priority in 2026.
The World Health Organization projects a shortage of 4.5 million nurses by 2030.
In the United Kingdom, 40% of general practitioners expect to leave the profession within the next five years.
Deloitte Global surveyed 180 C-suite executives from large health systems in August and September 2025.
Survey respondents were based in Australia, Canada, Germany, the Netherlands, the United Kingdom, and the United States.
Nearly 40% of today's job skills may become outdated because of AI and automation, according to the World Economic Forum.
Ransomware and supply chain attacks are emerging as major threats to health systems around the world.
Health system leaders across all six surveyed countries agreed that their 2026 strategies will be strongly influenced by financial pressures, workforce challenges, and cybersecurity risks.
market_data_points: 30% of surveyed health systems report operating generative AI at scale in select areas as of 2025.
Only 2% of surveyed health systems have deployed AI across their entire enterprise as of 2025.
64% of respondents cited AI-driven workflow standardization and automation as a source of cost savings in 2026.
55% of respondents see predictive analytics for workforce optimization as a savings opportunity in 2026.
49% of respondents expect cost benefits from tech-enabled patient engagement and remote monitoring in 2026.
WHO projects a global shortage of 4.5 million nurses by 2030.
180 C-suite executives from large health systems across six countries were surveyed in August–September 2025.
33% of US health system respondents expressed uncertainty about the 2026 industry outlook, up from 3% a year ago.
20% of US respondents expressed a negative industry outlook for 2026.
Only 13% of respondents expect operating costs to increase 'significantly' in 2026.
trend_signals: Health systems are prioritizing care model transformation, including expansion of outpatient services, digital offerings, and AI-driven patient follow-up.
Remote monitoring and virtual visits are expected to contribute to revenue growth by shifting care to lower-cost settings.
Tech-enabled patient engagement and remote monitoring are cited as a savings opportunity by 49% of respondents.
Preventive care and early detection are emerging as organizational priorities for 38% of non-US health system executives in 2026.
AI and agentic AI are seen as potential tools for risk stratification using genetics, environment, and lifestyle data.
Offshoring of IT and administrative tasks is becoming a common strategy for health systems to improve efficiency.
Cybersecurity investment is a top strategic priority for 2026 due to increasing ransomware and supply chain attacks on hospitals.
Workforce reskilling in AI and digital tools is identified as a critical imperative for health care workers.
Generative AI and agentic AI are expected to have limited major strategic impact on health systems in 2026 due to early adoption stages.
Whole-health and outcomes-based care models are identified as key components of future health care delivery.
competitive_mentions: US health systems face uncertainty due to ongoing concerns about tariffs, drug pricing, and regulatory changes affecting competitive positioning.
Eastern Europe is cited as a popular offshoring destination for health system IT and administrative tasks due to skilled workforce and lower labor costs.
regulatory_mentions: The United Kingdom does not allow the offshoring of patient-level data, restricting certain efficiency strategies for UK health systems.
US health system leaders cited ongoing uncertainties regarding tariffs, drug pricing, and regulatory changes as contributors to cautious outlook.
Fee-for-service payment models in the US incentivize volume over value, emphasizing treatment over prevention, contrasting with government-funded single-payer systems elsewhere.

sources.title: Wearable Medical Devices Market Size | Industry Report ...
key_facts: The global wearable medical devices market size was estimated at USD 42.74 billion in 2024.
The global wearable medical devices market is projected to reach USD 168.29 billion by 2030.
North America accounted for the largest revenue share of 35.76% in the wearable medical devices market in 2024.
The home healthcare segment accounted for the largest revenue share of 52.34% in 2024.
The diagnostic devices segment dominated the wearable medical devices market by type in 2024.
The strap/clip/bracelet segment accounted for the largest revenue share by site in 2024.
The therapeutic device segment is anticipated to witness the fastest CAGR of 26.71% throughout the forecast period.
The remote patient monitoring segment is anticipated to witness the fastest CAGR over the forecast period by application.
Asia Pacific is the fastest growing regional market for wearable medical devices.
The age-adjusted prevalence of diabetes among adults in the U.S. is estimated to increase from 10.7% in 2021 to 12.1% by 2030.
The increasing prevalence of neurological disorders is identified as a primary driver for the diagnostic devices segment.
Consumer-grade wearable medical devices dominated the market by grade type in 2024.
In February 2024, the U.S. FDA authorized the X-trades System M, a wireless wearable skin patch-based electrophysiological monitoring device for home use.
In January 2024, Cloud DX unveiled a contract to develop a wrist-based wearable capable of tracking ECG and various vital signs.
In October 2024, Oura revealed plans to acquire Sparta Science, a health and performance data analytics company.
In November 2024, Aktiia launched a cuffless blood monitoring bracelet in Canada as part of its European market expansion.
In December 2024, Bone Health Technologies announced pre-orders for Osteoboost, the first FDA-cleared non-drug wearable device to treat osteopenia in postmenopausal women.
In January 2024, FloPatch, a wearable ultrasound device by Flosonics Medical, was utilized in critical care units at St. Michael's Hospital for real-time blood flow assessment.
In November 2024, BioIntelliSense announced a study showing its FDA-cleared BioButton wearable device can detect early patient deterioration.
In February 2025, Washington State University researchers developed an algorithm to estimate and replace missing health data from wearable sensors.
market_data_points: Global wearable medical devices market size: USD 42.74 billion in 2024.
Projected market size: USD 168.29 billion by 2030.
North America revenue share: 35.76% in 2024.
Home healthcare segment revenue share: 52.34% in 2024.
Therapeutic devices segment CAGR: 26.71% (fastest among type segments) from 2025 to 2030.
U.S. diabetes prevalence projected to rise from 10.7% (2021) to 12.1% by 2030 per International Diabetes Federation.
Report covers historical data from 2018 to 2024 and forecasts from 2025 to 2030.
Report contains 300 pages (Report ID: 978-1-68038-724-7).
trend_signals: Rise of remote patient monitoring as a key growth driver for wearable medical devices.
Expansion of home healthcare as the dominant application segment, driven by regulatory approvals for home-use devices.
Increasing integration of wearables into clinical trials for real-time patient data collection.
Growing prevalence of neurological disorders driving demand for diagnostic wearable devices.
Surge in therapeutic wearable devices including pain relief, asthma management, and insulin management products.
Increasing M&A activity among wearable medical device companies to expand technological capabilities and product portfolios.
Expansion of smart shoe/footwear sensors as a significant emerging segment.
Cuffless blood pressure monitoring emerging as a product innovation area.
AI and algorithm development to enhance wearable sensor data reliability.
Regional geographic expansion by wearable device companies into new markets (e.g., Canada).
Rising health consciousness and affordability driving consumer-grade device adoption.
Robust pipeline of FDA-cleared therapeutic wearables accelerating market growth.
